title: How To Get Difficult Students To Listen To You https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2017/02/18/how-to-get-difficult-students-to-listen-to-you/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin explains that words alone rarely reach the most challenging students; what teachers actually need is influence, built through three guiding principles. First, avoiding friction — lecturing, scolding, threatening, or glaring — since each instance sabotages influence and creates an adversarial dynamic. Second, consistency, since selectively overlooking misbehavior to preserve rapport actually communicates untrustworthiness and undermines the very relationship a teacher is trying to build. Third, offering kindness without strings — smiles, hellos, and small gestures given without expectation of anything in return — which Linsin describes as having an almost magical way of unlocking rapport with even the most jaded students. Once these three elements are in place, he argues, a teacher's advice and encouragement stop being background noise and start genuinely resonating, sometimes for a lifetime.
points: Advice and encouragement have little effect on difficult students unless the teacher first builds genuine influence.
Avoiding friction — lecturing, scolding, threatening, glaring — is essential, since each instance damages influence.
Selectively overlooking misbehavior to preserve rapport backfires by signaling that the teacher's word cannot be trusted.
Consistent adherence to the classroom management plan, applied every day, is what actually builds trust and influence.
Unconditional kindness — given without manipulation or expectation of anything in return — unlocks rapport even with the most jaded students.
quotes: What you need is influence. Influence is that missing ingredient that will make your words matter and affect lasting change in behavior.
Every time you lecture, scold, threaten, argue with, or glare at difficult students you sabotage your influence with them.
But this communicates loud and clear that you can’t be trusted. It tells them that when you say something, it may or may not be true.
To build trust, and ultimately influence, you must be consistent day after day after day. You must follow your classroom management plan precisely as it’s written.

Extending simple kindness to your most difficult students, without manipulation, flattery, or expectation of receiving anything in return, has an almost magical way of unlocking powerful and influential rapport.
They appreciate this no-strings-attached interaction so much that despite themselves they’ll like and respect you.
They’ll stay with them and echo in their mind. Often for a lifetime.
